physicalDetails.detail: Long ears (she touches the tip of one to show how red the Ranger-Lord went). Rides at Jaina's right knee, close enough to reach her reins. Dismounts to fetch her arrow from the wolf's eye with a twist of the wrist.

Chapter 3: leans across to take the mage's mare by the cheekpiece and brings it round without a word; shifts her bow to the other hand when reporting; goes up the outside stair of the inn to the gallery; moves up to the sleeping mage's knee and hooks two fingers through the mare's cheek-strap; holds the far stirrup for the mage to mount; carries the right flank on the ride.

Chapter 4: rides on Jaina's right; reaches across to take the cheek-strap of Jaina's mare without turning her head; takes Jaina's weight at the waist at dismount and gives a cupped-hand step at mount; moves without sound ('as they did') to crouch across a truckle bed; her hands are 'quick and dry and warm'; wears a knife (cuts Jaina's blood-stiff linen off). Holds the staff's crystal against patients with one hand under the crystal and one round the silver wire.

Chapter 5: sits on the dry-stone wall with her bow across her knees, heels knocking the stones; rides at Jaina's knee, fist in the back of Jaina's coat after the mare goes down; sleeps instantly, mouth open sitting against a wall, or on the bracken with bow beside her; hands under Jaina's boot at the stirrup and mounting block; two fingers through the mare's cheek-strap; comes out yawning with bow strung and a crust in her other hand.

Chapter 6: rides the right of the road, her knee nearly touching Jaina's; turns round at her knee at the plain line; lifts Jaina down 'by the arms' and up at every stop since the sick village; dismounts first at the camp; drops back behind Jaina in narrow places and returns to her knee; moves her horse in until knees touch at the nosebleed and puts her hand over Jaina's on the reins; dug an apple out of her saddlebag below Strahnbrad.

Chapter 7 (Sylvanas POV): lifts Jaina down off the mare in the straw of the carter's yard; stands half a step behind Jaina in the gate queue close enough to take her weight; slides the pass inside the front of Jaina's coat; stands in the post doorway with her shoulder to the post, facing out; later at the shutter gap, shoulder to the frame, back turned to the room; walks on Jaina's right with her hand under her elbow and her eyes on the windows above; stops when Jaina stops.

voiceMarkers.detail: Quiet, dry, courteous: 'Lady Proudmoore'. Gossips gently to cheer the mage up ('She does that to everyone'). Flat and clipped in a fight ('Stag. Taking him.', 'Clear, right side.'). Low-voiced and tactful about the cow ('Not unless they mean to be home by milking, or else they--' and stops).

Chapter 3: reports one detail that lands ('There's a cradle in the house by the smithy with a blanket in it and no baby, Ranger-General. The blanket's been tucked.'); asks a clean practical question ('We did the houses already, Ranger-General?'); to the carter, warm and easy, 'friend': 'We passed nobody, friend. Not a living soul between here and the hills... The little one there spoke of a newer grain seller, though, so we'll keep an eye out for him going south, and if we see him we'll tell him you're looking. You'll get a better price going home full than going home empty, mind.'

Chapter 4: dry and teasing with the mage ('Steady.' said 'to the horse or to her'; 'Will you get down, or shall I fetch a ladder?'; 'If it bites me, Lady Proudmoore, I'm letting go.'), then the instructor register for the knot ('Loop over your thumb. Like that. Turn your wrist under. Tail through. Now take it in your teeth and set it.'; 'Now set it. Go on, Jaina. Bite it. It won't bite you back.'), plain on training ('All of us. In the first year. You do it with the left until you can, and then they make you do it with the right. We learn it so we can patch our own mistakes.'), quiet-plain at night ('Hold still. You've bled through.', 'Don't let Tobin see that. He'll want to bleed you as well.', 'Not on your own hand, you can't. Not yet. Tomorrow.'). Short worried imperative in the loft ('Jaina, leave it.'). Teasing in company: 'put that one of us ties a good knot, Captain, if there's room on the line', glancing at Cyndia. Snorts at Jaina's gunners' oath.

Chapter 5: the party's talker. 'Friend,' to a clerk; 'Master Corley' (after asking his name); easy, pleasant, steering: 'You keep a fire lit in here? In this? It's like standing in a boot.' Names Sylvanas to Corley ('the Ranger-General of Quel'Thalas') and reframes the rumour so he gives up the book. Admires a slate, a bean row, a miller's flour. Joke register: 'That man was paid by the loop, Jaina. I've seen less thread on a spindle.' 'There's a marrow out here I'd want to see a cart for, if I had to carry it.' 'Breakfast. I saved you the burnt end; it's the best bit, whatever Cyndia tells you.' Dry correction ('And that's the ones that kept a book.'). Says 'Jaina' aloud.

Chapter 7: quiet, no jokes. Reports in plain observed lines without turning round ('The man on the barrel's packed up his slate. There's a boy come up the street with a pole, lighting the lamps.'; 'Seven carts gone down the lane, Ranger-General. Loaded, every one. And one coming up empty, with the carter asleep on the seat; the horse knows the way better than he does.'); one-word acknowledgement 'Mine.'

beliefs.belief: The mage should be looked after as long as she is on the road, though not trusted: she steadies her reins when the mare panics but keeps two fingers on her bowstring when Jaina reaches into the satchel.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Unresolved; chapter 3 shows only care (cheek-strap, stirrup).

beliefs.belief: The carter is an ordinary road acquaintance who is owed a friendly, true answer: she saw no reason to withhold the girl's grain-seller remark or that they would watch for him going south.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Warm, true and not careless on page; plan says the answer is a plant that tells him the party has a witness and follows the grain-man south. The prose does not show Lyriel suspecting anything.

beliefs.belief: A hurt hand is no reason to be helpless: Farstriders learn one-handed knots 'so we can patch our own mistakes', and the mage can learn it too.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Held: Jaina does learn it by afternoon and dawn.

beliefs.belief: Jaina's read is worth paying for but not past the point of damage: 'Jaina, leave it.' (when Jaina keeps reading the shell).
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Jaina overrides her; the hand tears.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Hold the bend in Tenter Row: nobody comes down it at the party's backs, and the party comes out past her. Keep Jaina on her feet through the grab.
goalsAtChapterEnd.underlying: Keep the mage in one piece (she has caught her at every stop since Ch4).

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter6.active: Right-flank guard down the Andorhal approach; keep Jaina in the saddle, steady her mare, and get her down to rest if she'll allow it.
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter6.underlying: Keep the mage on her feet. Not shown doubting or connecting anything.

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter5.active: Right-flank guard on the south road into the hills; keep Jaina in the saddle and fed.
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter5.underlying: Keep the mage on her feet; make the party laugh in the dark (inferred).

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter4.active: Right-flank guard on the ride south; keep the mage upright and her hand clean; keep teaching her the knot.
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter4.underlying: Look after the mage as a person and not only as a prisoner (not shown; inferred from her acts).

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter3.active: Right-flank guard on the ride south; keep the mage in the saddle.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Quiet, level, working; at the shutter she watches the lane without turning. No jokes on the page; no sign of what is coming (alive; no foreshadowing).

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter6.state: Warm and watchful; worried about Jaina's body ('Your nose.', 'Get down a moment') and refused, and does not push. Shows no reaction to the tally-man's farewell (no link to her Ch3 exchange with the carter).

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter5.state: Warm, unbothered and tireless; asleep in seconds when allowed; cheerful with Jaina at breakfast; lets her flirt-with-clerks charm run to the point of work (Corley, the toll-keeper). Not shown doubting anyone.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter4.state: Easy, grinning at Jaina's dawn knot, warm; no visible shock at Tam's death (a lone worried 'Jaina, leave it.'). Pleased with Jaina and willing to tease her in public.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter3.state: Steady and easy; the one who talks to strangers, uncomplicated about the carter exchange.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Took Jaina's reins below the mare's chin at the stone line, then dropped back without comment.
Shot the stag and the wolf attacking Jaina's mare (arrow through the eye); stood over Jaina on the road while she read the doe.
Told Jaina that Sylvanas corrected the Ranger-Lord in front of his own captains at midsummer.

Calmed the mage's mare at the spook; swept the east side with Cyndia; held the inn gallery overlooking the north and west roads during the well read, then the bridge with the fourth ranger during the storehouse read; stood the first night watch with the fourth ranger; heard Cyndia's account of the girl's words facing the north road.

Answered the old carter's grain-man question with the true account (nobody passed; the girl mentioned a newer grain seller; they will watch for him going south; a better price going home full) and lowered her bow to do it.
Moved up beside the sleeping mage and took her mare's cheek-strap; held the stirrup at noon for her to mount.

Chapter 4: steadied the mare at the spook-and-cheek-strap and walked Jaina into the chapel; tied the horses; held the staff against patients so Jaina could read with her cheek; fetched the jug; warmed a bucket of water at the brazier; when Jaina could not tie Garran's bandage she crossed the bed without a sound and put her hands over Jaina's, taught the knot, and let go; later told her what Farstriders learn first.

Chapter 4: at the granary held a hand at the small of Jaina's back all the way up the stair and into the dark (pushed her on at the loft stair: 'because Lyriel pushed her on'); stayed close beside her while Cyndia and Sylvanas covered the boy; urged her 'Jaina, leave it.'; cut the boy's sleeve loose with Cyndia and hauled him down; covered Tam's face with her spare cloak; walked Jaina up Chapel Lane at a run with a hand at her back; deep in the night cut off, washed and rebound Jaina's torn left hand, tying the knot herself and biting it down; at dawn saddled up and gave Jaina a cupped-hand step.

Chapter 5: opened Corley's out-book by talking (turning the burn-and-fever news into a reason he should show it); called the yard count across to Cyndia; asked after the young fellow with the cart at the miller's; admired the slate; took Wick's ostler's and the toll-keeper's accounts by being sociable (beans); took the back of the overseer's house ('Back's clear. Kitchen garden, a well, washing on the line.'); held the wall at the shut depot; held Jaina on the mare through the night and mounted her at the block.

Chapter 6: lifted Jaina down and up; offered Jaina half an apple 'and half for her' (the mare, who has walked through more mud than a Silvermoon gardener sees in his life); at the nosebleed told her 'Jaina. Your nose.' and offered to hold the mare while Jaina sits on the wall; when Jaina said 'No.' she steadied Jaina's hand on the reins and let go when the mare stopped fighting the bit; did not press.

Chapter 7: watches the man on the wall at the gate while Jaina answers; takes the pass out of Jaina's fingers before she can fumble it; goes with Jaina and Corin through the inspection offices (Sylvanas's placement: 'Lyriel would watch the corridors and catch Jaina when she went over'); keeps watch at the shutter and counts carts; takes the Tenter Row bend ('Mine.').

abilitiesDemonstrated.ability: Best shot of the mounted detail: brought down a charging stag at full stretch and put an arrow in a wolf's eye while it struggled in ice.
Has crossed the Pass in midwinter (her own claim: with less ice under her).
Handling a skittish horse from the saddle, without a word.
Easy road conversation with a stranger; makes a stranger feel answered without giving offence.

Field medicine/instruction: one-handed bandage knot (loop over the thumb, wrist turned under, tail through, set with the teeth), taught in the first year to all Farstriders (left hand first, then right); washes and rebinds a split palm in the dark without stopping when the patient hisses.
Steady hands on a magical instrument: holds the staff's crystal and the silver wire against patients 'braced for it to do something sudden' without flinching; is not bitten.
Chapter 5: social extraction (clerks, millers, toll-keepers) by sympathy and small talk; keeps a human on a horse; spots details at the overseer's back (the marrow).
Chapter 6: physical care of an injured, half-numb rider (lifts, steadying hand, offers rest), steadying a frightened horse's rider by contact.

Chapter 7: perimeter watching with her back to the room (lamplighter, chalker, wagon traffic, cart counts and loads); physical support: keeps a hand under Jaina's elbow for a long walk across the city.

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Sylvanas (chapter 5)
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: 'Lyriel, with me.', 'Lyriel, get the mage down.', 'Lyriel, the back of that house.'

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Sylvanas
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: 'Lyriel' (orders: 'Cyndia, Lyriel, the east side.', 'Lyriel to the top of the lane.'; chapter 4: 'Lyriel. With the mage.' twice, 'Lyriel. With her.')

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Jaina
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: Chapter 4: 'Lyriel' aloud ('Lyriel. Bring me that jug.', 'Lyriel. The staff, please.', 'Will you hold this for me?'); thinks of her as Lyriel.

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Sylvanas (chapter 7)
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: 'Lyriel.' curt, first name, orders by event ('Lyriel. The bend in Tenter Row...').

howSheAddressesOthers.pattern: 'Jaina' aloud ('That man was paid by the loop, Jaina.'); no 'Lady Proudmoore'.
'Friend', then 'Master Corley'; friendly and flattering to the toll-keeper (beans) and miller (slate).

'Lady Proudmoore' twice early (dry, 'Will you get down...'; 'If it bites me, Lady Proudmoore...'); then 'Jaina' for the first time in mid-sentence during the knot lesson ('Go on, Jaina. Bite it.') and in the loft ('Jaina, leave it.'). Jaina notices the first use.
'Lady Proudmoore' (chapter 2); no direct address on page in chapter 3
'Ranger-General' when reporting or asking a question
'Captain' for Brask; Cyndia teased by glance, no address.
'Jaina' aloud ('Jaina. Your nose.', 'Get down a moment. Sit on the wall.'); no title.
No spoken address on the page; actions only.

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Face carefully on the road when Jaina dozes; glances at Cyndia after a joke; leans to take reins, then lets go; two fingers on her bowstring when Jaina reaches for the satchel; stands above the ditch with bow in hand.

Chapter 3: brings her bow up on the right at the bridge noise and lowers it to answer the carter; tips her head back toward the yard gate to indicate the girl; moves up and hooks two fingers through the mare's cheek-strap without being told.

Chapter 4: takes the cheek-strap 'without turning her head'; takes Jaina at the waist at dismount and lets go at once; crouches silently across a bed; puts her hands over Jaina's on a bandage then sits back on her heels; stands up with a bucket and walks off after telling the knot's purpose; grins at Jaina from the brazier and tips her head at the knot; hand at the small of Jaina's back as she walks; sits on the flags beside Jaina in the night and takes her hand without asking; shakes out a spare cloak and tucks it round a dead boy's face.

Chapter 6: turns round in the saddle at Jaina's statement; lifts Jaina by the arms; comes to the knee and puts her hand over Jaina's on the reins and holds until the mare calms; offers rest; drops back behind Jaina in narrow lanes and returns to the knee when it opens.

Chapter 7: shoulder to the doorpost facing out, then shoulder to the shutter frame at the gap; half a step off the shutter when Jaina rises in case she falls; moves in from the door to put a hand under Jaina's elbow before anyone asks.

knowledge.detail: Knows Sylvanas's habit of cutting off even the Ranger-Lord. Knows the cow should not be left bawling.
Chapter 3: heard Cyndia's account of the girl's words; knows the girl spoke of a newer grain seller; says she will watch for him going south. Does not appear to know anything else about the carter.

Chapter 4: knows the infirmary patients and what the mage found; the knot method and that Farstriders teach it; that the mage's left hand is torn (cut the linen off herself); that Tam died of poison from his collar. No sign she links the grain man with the carter.
Chapter 7: knows what the sample room cost Jaina; hears the table; sees seven loaded carts go down the lane. No sign she links anything to the carter's farewell.

arc.currentPosition: Chapter 4: the ranger who treats the mage as a person: first-name 'Jaina' arrives in the middle of a bandage lesson, she is the only member of the escort who touches Jaina's hands, and she is the one who teaches the one skill Jaina leaves with. Not yet shown to doubt or distrust Jaina. (Ch3 value: the one ranger who talks to strangers and to Jaina; that ease produces the carter's key exchange.)
arc.currentPositionNote_chapter6: Chapter 6: Jaina's keeper in the body; quiet this chapter (no jokes). Does not connect the tally-man's farewell to the Ch3 carter exchange; says nothing about it on page.
arc.currentPositionNote_chapter5: Chapter 5: still the party's easy talker and Jaina's keeper; the laugh in the wood and the saved burnt crust show the warmth is real and mutual; Cyndia does not join.
arc.currentPositionNote_chapter7: Chapter 7: Jaina's body-support and the party's perimeter eye; quiet, no jokes; alive and given a small specific competence (cart count; the lane-end hold). No foreshadowing of her death on the page.
